findings.reason: The protected source is already the canonical Floyd cycle-detection solution. Its first phase finds an interior meeting and its second phase resets one pointer to the first value to locate the cycle entrance. Slow and fast are conventional pointer concepts, the input is read-only, and no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 287 and its Python integer-list-to-integer contract. The Reference preserves the n + 1 versus [1,n] pigeonhole structure, one distinct repeated value with arbitrary multiplicity, all three examples and explanation absence, all four constraints, and both follow-up questions.

The immutable native source is tied to verified submission 2064311512. It and the app-local source have identical pointer initialization, one-step/two-step meeting phase, reset, equal-speed entrance phase, and return; only typing and the LeetCode class wrapper differ.

The legal 65/513/4097-element tiers place the repeated value last in the candidate range, forcing a repeated-count method to scan every preceding candidate while Floyd remains linear. The current source passes at +0.00 relative exponent and 0.99x largest ratio; a correct constant-space repeated-count control passes every output but fails only scaling at +0.68 and 9.86x.

The Approach now uses the implementation's exact reset to nums[0], keeps the functional-graph proof and modular meeting argument precise, accounts for read-only constant state, and distinguishes frequency storage, repeated counting, value-range binary search, sorting, and multiplicity above two.

The hash-bound public Reference remains verified against its reviewed source evidence, preserving all three examples in order with no invented explanations, all four constraints, both follow-up bullets after Constraints, and the zero-visual structure.
